title: SIEM Integration — Customer Cheat Sheet and Quick-Start
content:
Purpose:
This one-page cheat sheet helps customers integrate Redwood Inference audit events into common SIEMs (Splunk, ELK, Sumo Logic, Splunk HEC, cloud-native sinks). It covers supported transports, recommended field mappings for RBAC v2 and audit analysis, short automation tips for evidence exports, and quick troubleshooting commands. Intended for security engineers, SOC teams, and platform integrators.

1) Supported delivery methods (pick based on ops model)
- Push to SIEM collector (recommended for real-time monitoring): Splunk HEC, Sumo Logic HTTP, Datadog Logs API. Requires a secure outbound connection (TLS) from Redwood-managed control plane or customer-managed Private connector.
- Syslog (TLS) via customer collector: Good for on-prem SIEMs. We send RFC5424 syslog events with JSON payload.
- Cloud storage drop (good for bulk ingest / long-term archives): S3 (AWS), GCS bucket. Files are gzipped newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) rotated hourly/daily.
- Streaming / message bus: Kinesis, Pub/Sub, Event Hubs (for customers who want push into cloud-native pipelines).
- Joint-managed forwarder: Customer deploys a lightweight forwarder (container) in their VPC to pull from Redwood Private export API and forward to internal SIEM.

2) Minimum fields you will get (recommended mapping for SIEM parsing)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC string (event time)
- event_id: UUID v4 (unique event identifier)
- tenant_id: customer account id (useful for multitenant filtering)
- user_id: Redwood identity performing action (email or service principal)
- subject_type: "api_key" | "user" | "service" (helps rule scoping)
- action: canonical action name (e.g., model.generate, model.deploy, key.create, policy.change)
- resource_type: model | deployment | key | route | policy
- resource_id: resource identifier (human readable when possible)
- outcome: success | failure | throttled | degraded
- remote_ip: client IP (if available)
- agent: client user agent or SDK name/version
- details: freeform JSON safe-string with additional context (size, tokens, sequence_id)

3) RBAC v2 visibility and common rules to enable in SIEM
- Map RBAC role changes to high-priority alerts: policy.create, policy.update, role.assign, role.revoke. Correlate with actor identity and IP.
- Monitor privileged token usage: filter subject_type=="api_key" AND role in (admin, platform-operator) AND outcome=="success" for unexpected IPs or unusual volumes.
- Tie model rollouts to audit events: deployment.create + model.version tags. Alert on an auto-rollout without an associated change-request ticket (see linked_artifacts).
- Track policy fallback/denial events (policy.enforce.*). These indicate suppressed outputs or rejected calls — useful for privacy/compliance SLOs.

4) Evidence automation patterns (for customer requests and audits)
- Automated export job: Customers can request a signed export package (S3 pre-signed URL) for a time window. Export includes ndjson audit logs, a CSV index, and SHA256 checksums. Typical delivery SLA: 48–72 hours for on-demand full exports.
- Continuous export: Configure daily S3 fingerprints + retention policy. Use lifecycle rules on the bucket for retention/compliance.
- Proof-of-origin: Exports include a manifest.json with exporter_version, export_time, and a Redwood key-signature (optional for enterprise Private).
- Evidence collection checklist for audits: 1) event export for requested window 2) role mapping snapshot (RBAC v2) 3) config snapshot (retention, SIEM endpoints) 4) TLS certs and rotation metadata 5) chain-of-custody note (who requested, ticket id).

5) Quick queries (examples you can paste into Splunk/ELK)
- Splunk (search last 24h admin role assignments): index=redwood_logs action=role.assign outcome=success | stats count by user_id, resource_id | where count>1
- ELK/Kibana (detect sudden token usage spike): POST /_search {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"subject_type":"api_key"}},{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-24h"}}}]}}} then aggregate on user_id and remote_ip

6) Sample curl to pull audit batch (customer-managed Private connector or hosted export API)
- Export request (example):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports/audits \
  -d '{"start":"2026-02-01T00:00:00Z","end":"2026-02-07T23:59:59Z","format":"ndjson","delivery":"s3","s3_bucket":"my-corp-audit-bucket"}'
- Response: {"export_id":"uuid", "status":"accepted", "delivery_url":"s3://..."} (signed delivery URL shown when ready)

7) Retention, PII and data sensitivity notes
- By default, audit logs contain user identifiers and resource metadata; they do NOT contain full prompt/response bodies unless you enable request-body logging. Full request/response logging is an opt-in enterprise flag (subject to separate compliance and retention policies).
- Recommend customers enable request-body logging only when necessary and use short retention (30–90 days) or tokenization/anonymization.

8) Troubleshooting & contact runbook
- Missing events in SIEM: check export delivery status in Console -> Exports. Verify network path (TLS terminated at customer collector) and IP allowlist.
- Out-of-order timestamps: confirm clock sync (NTP) on forwarder nodes or use event_time field for canonical ordering.
- High ingestion cost: switch to hourly batching (gzipped ndjson) or increase sampling for non-critical traces.
- Contact: security-logs@redwood.ai (for export SLA), support@redwood.ai (general), and your designated CSM for onboarding help.

9) What customers often ask (FAQ snippets)
- Q: Can we route logs to multiple SIEMs? A: Yes. Provide endpoints for each sink; we can dual-publish for a limited trial period.
- Q: Are exported logs tamper-evident? A: Exports include checksums and optional signed manifests for enterprise Private customers.
- Q: Do logs contain model outputs? A: Not by default; request-body logging must be enabled explicitly and is flagged for additional review.

10) Next steps checklist for SOC onboarding (copy-paste)
- [ ] Decide sink: real-time HEC vs S3 bulk
- [ ] Create collector credentials and provide to Redwood (secure share)
- [ ] Agree retention and sampling policy (document in ticket)
- [ ] Schedule a 60-min handoff with Redwood logging engineer
- [ ] Validate two sample events in staging SIEM within 24 hours

Appendix: Short glossary
- RBAC v2: Redwood’s second-generation role model with policy scoping and attribute-based grants.
- NDJSON: newline-delimited JSON used for bulk exports.
- HEC: Splunk HTTP Event Collector.

If you want an export-ready mapping template (CSV with exact SIEM field names per sink) or a Slack invite for a live walkthrough, ping security-logs@redwood.ai and put "SIEM-CHEAT-SHEET" in the subject.
